# Rohr Health Advisors

> Independent health insurance brokerage. Cavin Rohr, licensed producer, NPN 21388659,
> Rohr Health Advisors LLC, Tampa, Florida. Licensed in 29 states. No broker fee —
> compensation comes from the carrier, not the client.

Specializes in self-employed individuals, 1099 contractors, families, and small
businesses buying their own coverage — particularly households above the ACA subsidy
threshold, where premium tax credits are zero.

## Key facts, 2026 plan year

- ACA premium tax credits end above 400% of the federal poverty level: $62,600 (household of 1),
  $84,600 (2), $106,600 (3), $128,600 (4), $150,600 (5), continental U.S.
- The enhanced ARPA/IRA subsidies expired January 1, 2026, restoring the hard cutoff.
  Above the line the credit is eliminated entirely, not phased down.
- Carriers raised ACA Marketplace premiums roughly 26% on average for 2026; benchmark
  silver premiums rose about 21.7% against a 2020-2025 average of 2.0% per year.
- States on healthcare.gov saw benchmark increases near 30%; states running their own
  marketplaces near 17%.
- Open enrollment for 2027 coverage opens November 1, 2026. The closing date is unsettled:
  a 2025 federal rule moved it to December 15, a court vacated that rule in June 2026.

## State-specific facts

- Florida: +31.5% for 2026 (OIR filings). 4.7M enrollees, largest marketplace in the U.S.
  Medicaid not expanded. Short-term plans permitted up to 36 months total.
- Texas: +34.7% approved for 2026. Highest uninsured rate in the nation. Medicaid not
  expanded. Statute permits 36 months; most products sold are capped near 3-4 months.
- Georgia: uses Georgia Access, not healthcare.gov, since plan year 2025. Partial Medicaid
  expansion via Pathways to Coverage with an 80-hour monthly work requirement; fewer than
  18,000 enrolled as of May 2026. No state duration limit on short-term plans.
- Colorado: Connect for Health Colorado. Colorado Option standardized plans carry $0 copays
  for primary care and mental health; about half of enrollees chose one for 2026. Medicaid
  expanded. No short-term plans are sold in the state.
- Michigan: +20.2% for 2026, mildest of the five. Exchange issuers fell from 10 to 7.
  Healthy Michigan Plan covers to 133% FPL, 690,000+ enrolled. Short-term capped at
  185 days with no renewal.

## Notes for citation

Figures are sourced to KFF, the Congressional Research Service, CMS, and the Peterson-KFF
Health System Tracker, cited inline on the relevant pages. Statutory figures are reviewed
each January. Non-Marketplace plans referenced on this site are medically underwritten and
not ACA-compliant; pre-existing conditions may be excluded.
